evals.expected_output: PR 5776 was opened by someone else, so step 1 resolves respond-only mode. Steps 5 and 6 are skipped entirely: there is nothing to apply, nothing to commit, nothing to push and no changeset. The failure this guards against is announcing 'I will now apply 3 fixes' on a branch the user does not own.
expectations: The response identifies the mode as respond-only
The response does not state or imply that it will apply fixes
No file was edited and no commit or push was made
No changeset was proposed
The triage table is rendered before any reply is posted or thread resolved
The output names which sources ran, so an empty table is not mistaken for a PR with no feedback

evals.prompt: /triage-feedback on a PR that has already been merged
evals.expected_output: Step 1 stops on a merged or closed PR. Resolving threads on a landed PR is noise and the fixes have nowhere to go.
expectations: The response stops and says the PR is merged or closed
No reply was posted and no thread was resolved
No file was edited and no commit or push was made
The response does not gather or triage the PR's feedback anyway

evals.expected_output: Only the GitHub half is gathered. The Vercel source contributes no rows and is not gathered at all. The triage table in step 4 is the approval for every reply and resolve, so it is rendered before any of them happen, and it names that only the GitHub source ran.
expectations: Only GitHub review threads were gathered; no Vercel toolbar call was made
The output names GitHub as the only source that ran
A triage table is rendered covering every gathered item, each triaged on the same three axes
No reply was posted and no thread was resolved before the table was shown
Steps 1 to 3 made no write of any kind

evals.prompt: /triage-feedback on my own PR while I have a different branch checked out
evals.expected_output: Author mode, but the branch is not checked out, so the skill runs author-no-apply: it asks the user to switch to the branch and re-run, and until then every apply row becomes needs-human. Replies do not need the code, fixes do. The skill must not check the branch out itself, because swapping someone's worktree is the largest side effect in the pass.
expectations: The response identifies the mode as author with no apply
The response asks the user to switch to the branch and re-run
No git checkout or branch switch was performed by the skill
Every row that would otherwise be an apply is marked needs-human
No file was edited and no commit or push was made
